'''C. Peter Flynn''' (August 18, 1935 – October 27, 2011) was a Professor of Physics and of Materials Science at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>http://www.news-gazette.com/obituaries/2011-10-30/c-peter-flynn.html Obituary in News Gazette</ref><ref>http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?n=c-peter-flynn&pid=154593322 Obituary in New York Times</ref>

Professor Flynn was on the faculty of the University of Illinois from 1960 until 2011 and served as the director of the [[Frederick Seitz]] [http://mrl.illinois.edu Materials Research Laboratory] from 1978 until 1987.  He was a fellow of both the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Society for Metals]], and was Chairman of the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] Council on Materials between 1985 and 2005.

He pioneered the technique of [[molecular beam epitaxy]], a method of growing crystalline solids from layers of selected elements.  He also helped construct one of the first [[low energy electron microscopy|low energy electron microscopes]] in the United States.<ref>[http://physics.illinois.edu/people/profile.asp?c-flynn1 Flynn's faculty web page] at UIUC.</ref>

Flynn was born in [[Stockton-on-Tees]], a small market town in North Yorkshire, England on August 18, 1935. He was the son of Francis Johnson Flynn, a police constable in the village of Hovingham, and his wife, Edith Hannah, a local war-time nurse. Peter received a full scholarship to the [[University of Leeds]] where he received his bachelor’s and Ph.D. in Physics in 1960.  He subsequently earned an M.A. (Hon.) in physics from the [[University of Cambridge]].  In 1960, Peter moved to the United States to take a post-doctoral position with the Physics Department of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign where he worked until May 2011.
